feasibility_reasoning: The mechanism works, but not as specified. On the existing .output (checkout f261c49), `node scripts/performance/check-document-weight.ts` passes all 19 metrics: HTML 391114 B raw / 54475 B gzip. `bun run scripts/performance/check-document-weight.ts` exits 1 with `htmlGzipBytes 55567 > 55565`, because under bun every gzip metric reads about 2% higher (boot 488589 vs 485279 B). The budgets were measured with node's zlib (documentWeight.ts:135 and :353 gzipSync). The script also imports untracked ./artifactServer.ts (check-document-weight.ts:28-35), which is not in the change's file list, and the unit test imports untracked ./lighthouseReport.ts (document-weight.test.mjs:19). CI wiring: the step only makes sense in job `build` after build:smoke (ci.yml:1118-1124). CI builds with VITE_SUPABASE_URL set to placeholder.supabase.co or the secret; SSR is still served by the fixture because homeFixture.ts:97-103 matches any *.supabase.co host. The only env-dependent bytes are window.__SUPABASE_CONFIG__: about 170 B gzip, inside the 1090 B headroom. The preconnect origin is a constant (rootHead.ts:65,112). Node 24.19 in CI strips types, so the .ts imports load. prettier, eslint and tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json are clean on the draft files, and node --test on document-weight.test.mjs passes 7/7. verify-static.ts EXCLUDED needs the new entry, as the plan says. Risk is understated: the count budgets have zero headroom (inlineStyleCount 50/50, modulepreloadCount 25/25, linkHeaderEntries 31/31, preloadDuplicates 22/22, imgFetchpriorityHigh 9/9). Any legitimate new widget, or a Lovable-bot commit straight to main, turns `build` red. Enriching e2e/fixtures/first-visit.json also forces a manual raise of the budgets, which the "only down" rule forbids. There is no SSR, hydration, i18n, SEO or editor impact because nothing in src/ changes.
blocking_issues: The file list leaves out scripts/performance/artifactServer.ts, which check-document-weight.ts:28-35 imports, and lighthouseReport.ts, which document-weight.test.mjs:19 imports. Committing only the listed files gives module-not-found in CI. artifactServer.ts is shared with lighthouse-local.mjs, so the change must also say which change owns it.

The runtime must be node, not bun. The house-convention script `bun run scripts/performance/check-document-weight.ts` fails on the baseline today (htmlGzipBytes 55567 > 55565) because the budgets were measured with node zlib. package.json needs `"check:document-weight": "node scripts/performance/check-document-weight.ts"`, the same pattern as check:first-visit-regression at package.json:96. The workflow can still call `bun run check:document-weight` for check:gate-coverage. The alternative is to re-ratchet the budgets under CI's bun 1.2.23.
The workflow step has to be in job `build`, directly after the build:smoke step (ci.yml:1118-1124), and exactly once per job. Anywhere else it measures the cloudflare .output or finds no artifact.
verify-static.ts EXCLUDED needs a check:document-weight entry. Without it, verify:static goes red on any machine that has no .output.
effect_reasoning: The gate ships zero bytes to the browser, so the direct score change is 0, as the change itself claims. It gates fixture numbers (54.5 KB gzip HTML), not production (78 KB gzip / 569 KB raw). Its 2% gzip headroom is about 1.1 KB, roughly 5 ms of transfer at 1.6 Mb/s (about 200 KB/s), so regressions inside the headroom do not move the score. What it really protects is structure: the count metrics and new inline blocks. Its value is the size of the waves it locks in. Example: html-weight takes inline CSS from 133 KB to 20 KB, cutting about 25-30 KB gzip of HTML. At about 200 KB/s that is roughly 0.15 s of FCP/LCP on mobile, about 1-2 points, which the gate then keeps from coming back. No cheaper gate does the same job. check:ssr-budgets is static. check:bundle does not see HTML or inline CSS (and gates boot gzip only at 579 KB, versus 483.4 KB here). Lighthouse mode C errors only on CLS and TBT. It also closes PA-F3 by gating bootClosureRawBytes at 1599.4 KB.
corrected_estimate: 0 points directly; it locks in gains only after the html-weight and lcp-path waves land. Risk is medium, not low, because of the zero-headroom count budgets, direct bot commits to main, and the bun/node gzip mismatch. Effort M stands (most of it is CI wiring and committing the dependencies).
better_alternative: Keep the change, with four fixes: commit artifactServer.ts with it (plus lighthouseReport.ts if the unit test is wired), point the package script at node, give the count metrics at least +1 headroom or document a re-measure procedure in _comment for legitimate widget additions, and note in _comment that check:bundle (bun) and this gate (node) report boot gzip with different zlib implementations.
